title: Custom Colors
definition: Defining brand-specific color palettes within Tailwind's configuration file.
simpleExplanation: Giving names to HEX codes. Instead of remembering `#FF5733`, you name it `primary`. Tailwind then does the magic of creating all the background, text, border, and ring classes for it.
realWorldExample: Creating semantic color names like `success`, `warning`, and `danger` instead of using `green`, `yellow`, and `red`.

basic: If you add a color called `primary: '#123456'` to your config, what class do you use to make text that color?
intermediate: How do you define CSS Variables (like `var(--color-primary)`) inside `tailwind.config.js`?

answers.question: CSS Variables?
answers.answer: You just write the CSS variable exactly as a string: `primary: 'var(--color-primary)'`. This is incredibly powerful for letting users change themes dynamically at runtime.
